source.work: Next.js App Router docs, linking and navigating
source.paraphrase: Internal navigation uses the Link component so the router can prefetch and transition client-side instead of reloading the page.

invariants.why: A plain anchor to an internal route forces a full document reload and skips prefetching, losing the client-side navigation the router exists for.
invariants.fixHint: Replace the anchor with Link from next/link. Keep anchors for external URLs only.
invariants.avoid: This advisory policy checks actual anchor nodes with literal root-relative href attributes, including expression-wrapped strings, anywhere in JSX. It ignores CMS HTML strings, unrelated attributes, external and protocol-relative URLs, an anchor with target="_blank", and an anchor with a download attribute. Full reloads can be intentional; do not promote this suggestion without the project's navigation contract.

source.paraphrase: The App Router owns the document through the root layout. next/document belongs to the Pages Router and has no effect under app.

invariants.why: A Document import inside app/ silently does nothing while suggesting the Pages Router still controls the shell, so document changes never apply.
invariants.fixHint: Move document-level markup into the app root layout and declare head data with the metadata export.
invariants.avoid: Re-exporting next/document from a shared module so app files keep importing it indirectly. A string that mentions next/document without importing it is not an import.

source.work: Next.js App Router docs, programmatic navigation
source.paraphrase: Next routers accept href strings. A template or route helper can make the destination easier to read; concatenation alone is not a correctness violation.

invariants.why: This optional readability policy observes concatenated destinations on recognized Next routers. Valid href strings remain valid; the syntax does not prove an unsafe destination or a typed-route failure.
invariants.fixHint: Use a template or the project's tested route helper when this improves clarity. Validate untrusted destinations under the project's routing contract; interpolation alone is not a security fix.
invariants.avoid: Checks cover imported Router and directly imported useRouter calls or same-block const receivers. Array.push, arbitrary injected push methods, indirect aliases, cross-scope bindings and dynamic receiver ownership are not inferred. Keep project routing safety in a reviewed assertion rather than enforcing a preferred spelling.

source.work: Migrating to Cache Components, https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components; Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model), https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components
source.paraphrase: Without Cache Components, revalidate = false is the documented default and caches indefinitely. With cacheComponents enabled, exporting revalidate from a page, layout, or route errors. Replace a positive interval with cacheLife inside use cache, and delete revalidate = 0.

invariants.why: A literal false or a number is legal in the previous model, so it is not reported unless the root Next config enables Cache Components. Then Next.js rejects the export at build time.
invariants.fixHint: Remove the revalidate export. For data that should be cached, add use cache and cacheLife. For data that must run every request, leave it outside use cache.
invariants.avoid: Only an exported revalidate on a page, layout, or route is matched, and only when the first existing root next.config.js, next.config.mjs, or next.config.ts sets cacheComponents to literal true. A 'use client' file is left to NEXT-SERVER-EXPORT-001. A local variable, a fetch next.revalidate option, and a commented or nested flag are not this export. Computed cacheComponents values are not detected.

source.work: Next.js App Router API reference, useRouter, https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-router
source.paraphrase: In the App Router, useRouter must come from next/navigation, not next/router. Using the Pages Router hook under app throws 'NextRouter was not mounted'.

invariants.why: next/router needs the Pages Router context, which app/ does not provide, so the component throws when it renders.
invariants.fixHint: Import useRouter from next/navigation. Read the path with usePathname and the query with useSearchParams. Shared components that must run under both routers can use next/compat/router.
invariants.avoid: Only the exact next/router literal in a value import, re-export, require or import() inside app/ or src/app/ is flagged. Type-only imports, next/compat/router, next/navigation and files under pages/ are allowed. Components outside app/ that the App Router renders are not traced.

source.work: Route Segment Config, https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config; cacheComponents, https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents; Migrating to Cache Components, https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components
source.locator: Version history v16.0.0; runtime; dynamic, revalidate, and fetchCache
source.paraphrase: Route segment options and generateStaticParams apply only in Server Components. When cacheComponents is enabled, dynamic, dynamicParams, revalidate, and fetchCache are removed, and runtime is unsupported, including runtime = 'nodejs'.

invariants.why: Exporting server route segment options or generateStaticParams from a file marked 'use client' either fails the Next.js build or is silently ignored. With cacheComponents enabled, Next.js also errors on server exports of dynamic, dynamicParams, revalidate, fetchCache, and runtime.
invariants.fixHint: Move the export to a Server Component page, layout, or route. When cacheComponents is enabled, delete dynamic, dynamicParams, revalidate, fetchCache, and runtime. Cache with use cache and cacheLife, or leave the data uncached.
invariants.avoid: Direct variable exports, function exports, and export list specifiers in 'use client' page, layout, and route files are matched, including dynamicParams and fetchCache. Local unexported variables pass. When the first existing root next.config.js, next.config.mjs, or next.config.ts sets cacheComponents to literal true, server files are also checked for dynamic, dynamicParams, fetchCache, and runtime. preferredRegion, maxDuration, generateStaticParams, ensureStatic, and instant are not flagged on the server. A nested or computed flag is not treated as enabled. An empty generateStaticParams return is a separate build error and is not matched.

source.work: Next.js 16 upgrade guide, https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16; Proxy file convention, https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy
source.locator: middleware to proxy; Migration to Proxy
source.paraphrase: The named export middleware is deprecated. proxy.ts must export a function named proxy, or a default export. The guide recommends renaming a default export too, and that remains a recommendation.

invariants.why: Proxy runs the default export or the export named proxy. A named middleware export is not that function, so the request reaches the route with none of the redirect, rewrite, or header changes.
invariants.fixHint: Rename the named export to proxy: export function proxy(request) {}. A default export may keep its local name. https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy
invariants.avoid: Only proxy.ts and src/proxy.ts (and the same .js, .jsx, .tsx, .mjs, .cjs names) are read. export function, export const, and export { x as middleware } are flagged. export default function middleware is not, because a default export is a supported proxy function. A local unexported function named middleware passes. The rule runs only when next is declared entirely on 16 or newer.

source.work: Next.js 16 upgrade guide, https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16; Next.js 15 middleware runtime, https://nextjs.org/docs/15/app/api-reference/file-conventions/middleware
source.paraphrase: The middleware filename is deprecated in favor of proxy. Proxy runs on Node.js and cannot set a runtime. Middleware defaults to the Edge runtime; Node.js is selected with export const config = { runtime: 'nodejs' }. Edge middleware stays in middleware.ts.

invariants.why: A Node.js middleware.ts file is the deprecated filename for the runtime proxy.ts now owns. Leaving it splits request interception across two conventions. Edge middleware is still the supported middleware.ts file.
invariants.fixHint: Rename middleware.ts to proxy.ts, export proxy, and delete config.runtime. Keep middleware.ts when the file should stay on the Edge runtime, which is the default when config.runtime is not "nodejs". https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16
invariants.avoid: Only middleware.ts and src/middleware.ts (and the same JavaScript extensions) are read. The finding is the exported config object's own runtime: "nodejs" pair, in either quote style. A matcher-only config, runtime: "edge", and a nested runtime string are not the Node.js opt-in. The rule runs only when next is declared entirely on 16 or newer, and it warns rather than denies because the file still runs.
